=== DOCS-VERIFICATION 2026-06-07 (BEFORE writing) ===
(1) trino.io/docs/467/functions/window.html — verbatim: 'Window functions perform calculations across rows of the query result. They run after the HAVING clause but before the ORDER BY clause.' This establishes the clause-evaluation order that BANS window functions in WHERE (WHERE runs FIRST, before window functions). CONFIRMED: window functions NOT allowed in WHERE clause.
(2) WebSearch confirmed: nested window functions REJECTED by Trino 467 StatementAnalyzer (also referenced in resources/23-sql-best-practices-olap.md line 876 — PR #23929 / Issue #24163 already pinned for the ORDER-BY-nested-window case; same rejection rule covers the general nested-window case).
(3) trinodb/trino issue #7885 + WebSearch CONFIRMED: Trino does NOT support DISTINCT inside window functions — COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) OVER (...) is REJECTED at analysis time. Limitation matches Redshift / SQL Server.
(4) Aggregate FILTER (WHERE ...) clause CONFIRMED at trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html verbatim: 'The FILTER keyword can be used to remove rows from aggregation processing with a condition expressed using a WHERE clause.' But the FILTER predicate is a row-level WHERE-like predicate evaluated alongside the aggregate's row-by-row consumption — a window function cannot appear inside it for the same evaluation-order reason that bans windows in WHERE. CONFIRMED: window inside aggregate FILTER REJECTED.
(5) trino.io/docs/467/functions/hyperloglog.html CONFIRMED verbatim: approx_set(x) -> HyperLogLog 'creates a HyperLogLog sketch'; merge(HyperLogLog) -> HyperLogLog 'returns the HyperLogLog of the aggregate union of the individual hll HyperLogLog structures' — i.e. merge() IS the aggregate that unions HLL sketches across rows; cardinality(hll) -> bigint extracts the approximate distinct count. CAST(... AS HyperLogLog) round-trip from varbinary required because Iceberg/Parquet has no native HLL encoding.
(6) The wrap-the-window-in-a-CTE remedy CONFIRMED — universal SQL semantics: a CTE/subquery in FROM exposes ONLY its projected SELECT-list columns; once a window expression is projected as a plain alias, the outer query sees a plain column, not a window — outer WHERE/FILTER/CASE comparisons against the projected alias are legal. This is the docs-correct fix for all three iter636 A4 bad forms.

  - GENERAL SCOPE RULE paragraph: a CTE/subquery in FROM exposes ONLY its projected SELECT-list columns; once you project the window as `cust_max`, the outer query sees a plain column — universal SQL semantics that makes the wrap-then-compare fix work.
